findings.title: Test doesn't wait for the sandboxed process to actually exit
findings.detail: agentsOutliveTheThreadThatStartedThem() calls process.terminate() but never awaits process.waitUntilExit() (or polls process.isRunning) before the test returns. terminate() only requests SIGTERM asynchronously; the bwrap/sleep process can keep running for some time after the test completes, which can leave a stray sandboxed process (with --unshare-pid) alive in CI past this test, unlike the sibling test homeShowsOnlyTheToolsInsideBubblewrap which does call waitUntilExit().

findings.title: Agent cleanup now depends entirely on external systemd config, unverified in code
findings.detail: Dropping --die-with-parent removes the only in-process guarantee that a sandboxed agent dies with its parent. The comment states systemd's default KillMode=control-group now does this job, and Runner/oby-runner.service relies on that implicit default (no explicit KillMode= line), but nothing in the codebase enforces or checks it. If the runner is ever run outside that specific systemd unit (local dev, a different service manager, a manually started process), a crashed runner can leave bwrap sandboxes - with read access to the whole host filesystem and devices - running indefinitely with no code path left to reap them.
